extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third‑party requesters, patent owners, and USPTO examiners handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) guidance describing statutory/regulatory requirements and office practice for requesting, processing, conducting, and concluding inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Prior Art (35 U.S.C. 301; 37 CFR 1.501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office prior art consisting of patents or printed publications believed to have a bearing on patentability; if the person explains in writing the pertinency and manner of applying such prior art to at least one claim, the citation and explanation become part of the official file. The identity of the citer may be kept confidential on written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations should either (1) reflect that a copy has been mailed to the patent owner at the address in § 1.33(c) or (2) if service is not possible, be filed in duplicate. See MPEP §§ 2202–2206 and 2208 for making and handling citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of Prior Art Citations During Inter Partes Reexamination (37 CFR 1.902)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of 37 CFR 1.501 prior art citations when an inter partes reexamination is pending depends on timing and source of the citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted prior to an order to reexamine, citations will be considered in the reexamination. If after an order: (A) patent owner citations normally considered if timely before certificate issues; (B) third‑party requester citations considered if submitted as part of required comments under §§ 1.947/1.948 or in a properly filed request under §§ 1.915/1.510; (C) other citations are retained until reexamination concludes and then placed in the patent file. See 37 CFR 1.902.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Reexamination Eligibility (statutory applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination is available only for patents issuing from original applications filed on or after November 29, 1999; patents issuing from applications filed prior to that date are not eligible for the optional inter partes reexamination (only ex parte reexamination applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'original application' includes utility, plant, and design first filings, continuations, divisionals, continuations‑in‑part, CPAs, and national stage filings, but excludes reissue applications. An RCE filed on or after May 29, 2000 in an application originally filed before Nov 29, 1999 does not make that patent eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Scope in Inter Partes Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art considered during inter partes reexamination is limited to prior patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other types of evidence (e.g., non‑printed oral evidence) are not within the statutory scope for prior art in inter partes reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question (SNQ) of Patentability Required (35 U.S.C. 312(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'substantial new question of patentability' must be present for the Office to order inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office initially determines whether the request presents a substantial new question; if so, reexamination is ordered. The request must point out each SNQ and provide a detailed explanation of pertinency and application to each claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision Timeframe on Request (statutory timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office must decide whether to grant or deny a request for inter partes reexamination within three months of its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordered, the remainder of the proceedings is to proceed with 'special dispatch' within the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑Party Participation and Procedural Differences
rubrics_metrics.description: If ordered, the reexamination proceeding is essentially inter partes in nature: third‑party requesters may participate throughout, there is an action closing prosecution (ACP) and a right of appeal notice rather than a traditional final rejection, and special time periods/forms apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third‑party requester has appeal rights to the Board and, for proceedings commenced on/after Nov 2, 2002, to the Federal Circuit; prosecution features differ from regular examination (limitations on rejections, ACP, right of appeal notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Enlargement of Claim Scope by Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the patent claims cannot be enlarged by amendment during inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that broaden claim scope are not permitted; only narrowing/amendments that do not enlarge the scope are acceptable consistent with statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access and Electronic File Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination and patent files are open to the public, but reexamination files are scanned to provide an electronic copy for public access; the paper file is not available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All public access to and copying of reexamination proceedings may be had from the electronic copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Litigation Tactics and Restricted Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination statute, regulations, and published procedures do not countenance 'litigation tactics'; parties are expected to conduct themselves accordingly and to use only submissions provided for by the regulations unless an appropriate petition is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions not provided for by the regulations should be filed with an appropriate petition or not filed. Multiple submissions such as a reply and a sur‑reply that are not provided for are discouraged. Parties must adhere to 37 CFR 10.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Requirements for Request (37 CFR 1.915(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for inter partes reexamination must include specified parts and meet defined content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required parts (per 37 CFR 1.915(b)): (1) identification of the patent number and every claim for which reexamination is requested; (2) citation of patents/printed publications presented to provide an SNQ; (3) a statement pointing out each SNQ with a detailed explanation of pertinency and manner of applying the citations to every claim; (4) copy of every relied‑on patent/printed publication with English translations of pertinent parts of non‑English documents; (5) a copy of the entire patent (front page, drawings, specification/claims) and any disclaimers/certificates (single‑side pages); (6) certification that a copy of the request was served on the patent owner (name/address indicated) or, if service not possible, duplicate copy supplied to the Office; (7) certification that estoppel provisions of § 1.907 do not prohibit the inter partes reexamination; (8) a statement identifying the real party in interest to the extent necessary for subsequent filers to determine privy status. If filed by an attorney/agent identifying another party, a power of attorney or representative capacity under § 1.34 is required (see 1.915(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Requirement for Request (37 CFR 1.915(a); 1.20(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must be accompanied by the fee for requesting inter partes reexamination set forth in § 1.20(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee or required content is missing, the requester will be notified and generally given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. Failure to comply results in the request not receiving a filing date and being placed in the patent file as a citation if it complies with § 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Date of Request (37 CFR 1.919)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a request for inter partes reexamination is the date on which the request satisfies all the requirements set forth in § 1.915.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete requests initially may be given an opportunity to be completed; only when all requirements are met is the filing date established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrevocability of Request after Receipt of Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: After the request for inter partes reexamination, including the entire fee, is received by the Office, abandonment, withdrawal, or striking of the request is generally not possible regardless of who requested it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited exceptions exist (e.g., after a final court decision where all claims are held invalid, a reexamination order may be vacated — see MPEP § 2686.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons Eligible and Statutory Prohibitions (37 CFR 1.913 and 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 1.907, any person other than the patent owner or its privies may file a request for inter partes reexamination of a patent issued from an original application filed on or after Nov 29, 1999, on the basis of prior patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.907 enumerates prohibitions: once an order is issued, the requester (and privies) may not file subsequent inter partes requests until a certificate issues (unless authorized by Director); a final adverse civil decision under 28 U.S.C. 1338 precludes later inter partes requests on issues the party raised or could have raised; a final decision in an inter partes proceeding favorable to patentability precludes that requester (and privies) from later requests on issues that were or could have been raised. The requester must certify compliance with § 1.907; that certification is prima facie and the Office does not generally investigate beyond it unless facially challenged by the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Real Party in Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a statement identifying the real party in interest to the extent necessary for a subsequent requester to determine whether that person is a privy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The included certification that the requester is not barred under 1.907 constitutes a prima facie showing; Office will only investigate further if a facial challenge is raised by the patent owner that facially establishes the requester is barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative Requirements for Requester (37 CFR 1.915(c); 1.34; 1.32(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an attorney or agent files an inter partes request identifying another party, the attorney/agent must have a power of attorney from that party or be acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34; powers of attorney may name as representative only inventors or registered patent practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To act in representative capacity, the attorney/agent must set forth registration number, name and signature. Filing of the power of attorney is desirable but processing of the request will not be delayed for its absence. Proof of authority may be required if a question is raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Requesting — Period of Enforceability and Exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A third‑party requester may file during the period of enforceability of the patent; the Office set the enforceability period by rule and it is determined by adding six years to the date on which the patent expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent expiration for a utility patent takes into account term, maintenance fees, disclaimers, term extensions/adjustments under 35 U.S.C. 154, premarket regulatory extensions under 35 U.S.C. 156, and other relevant information. If litigation is instituted within the statute of limitations period, requests may be filed after the statute of limitations has expired so long as the patent remains enforceable against someone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel Effect on Third‑Party Requester
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercising the inter partes option is conditioned on the third‑party requester accepting a statutory estoppel against subsequent review (by the Office or by a Federal Court) of issues that were or could have been raised in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estoppel limits are aimed at preventing harassment of patent owners. The requester must certify that the estoppel provisions of § 1.907 do not prohibit the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and Processing on Requests (CRU/TC handling; timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is granted, reexamination is ordered and proceedings are processed with specified forms, panel review, and time reporting; decisions and workflows are subject to Office procedure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual details fee processing, assignment, transfer, time reporting, criteria for deciding requests, claims considered, prior art basis for determination, and examples of decisions. Panel review is conducted at each stage of examination (except non‑merits actions); appeal conferences are panel reviews prior to Examiner’s Answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate Content and Format
rubrics_metrics.description: At conclusion, an inter partes reexamination certificate is issued and formatted similarly to a patent title page with specific additions: title 'INTER PARTES REEXAMINATION CERTIFICATE' with ordinal number; certificate number equals original patent number plus kind‑code suffix (C1, C2, ...); filing date/number of the request noted as 'Reexamination Request'; 'Reexamination Certificate for' identifies original patent; INID codes used similarly to patents; list of prior art documents limited to those in reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate will identify claims confirmed as patentable, canceled, disclaimed, and not examined; new claims printed in italics, amended claims printed with italics and bracketing; prior court decisions identified; example of kind code handling when prior B1 certificates exist is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening Rights for Amended/New Claims (35 U.S.C. 316)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following inter partes reexamination has the same intervening rights effect as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects persons who made, purchased, used, or imported items, or made substantial preparations therefor, prior to issuance of the certificate. The manual cites cases and parallels to reissue/ex parte reexamination intervening rights doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding Reexamination Proceedings (ways to conclude)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination proceedings may be concluded by (A) denial or vacatur of the request, (B) issuance of a reexamination certificate under § 1.997(b), or (C) merging with a reissue proceeding and grant of a reissue patent where the reissue patent constitutes the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing instructions vary depending on conclusion type: forwarding files to CRU, assigning appropriate status codes (e.g., 820, 822), partial refunds where applicable, and coordination with reissue processing when merged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Review and Quality Assurance (CRU SPE / TC QAS and RLA review)
rubrics_metrics.description: After examiner action and clerical processing, the Central Reexamination Unit Supervisory Patent Examiner (CRU SPE) or Technology Center Quality Assurance Specialist (TC QAS) procedurally reviews the examiner’s action for compliance with statute/regulations and for completeness; the Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) reviews for correct application of reexamination law and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review is also made prior to issuing Office actions (see MPEP § 2671.03). After NIRC and termination of prosecution, the Office of Patent Legal Administration screens for errors and proper preparation before issuing certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Specified USPTO Forms in Inter Partes Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain PTO forms must be used by the Office in inter partes reexamination processing (e.g., notices of incomplete request, notices of assignment, order granting/denying request, office action forms, Action Closing Prosecution form, Right of Appeal Notice, NIRC, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public Request for Reexamination Transmittal Form (PTO/SB/58) is provided but not mandatory. The manual enumerates PTOL form numbers and intended uses; proper form use is required for correct processing.
